componentSets.name: Drawer
componentSets.description:
A drawer is a secondary content surface that slides in from one edge of a layout. Use drawers for supplemental info and simple actions related to the main content.


Overlay drawer
An overlay drawer is an intrusive surface that obscures all or part of the main page content. Use overlay drawers to draw more attention to the content in the drawer.


Inline drawer﻿
An inline drawer is a passive surface that sits side-by-side with main page content. Use inline drawers when it’s helpful to view and interact with page content and drawer content at the same time.


For short information that’s related to a specific part of the main layout, a drawer may be overwhelming. Try a tooltip or a popover instead. If you need people to confirm an action they’re trying to take, use a dialog.

componentSets.name: Dropdown
componentSets.description:
A dropdown lets people choose one or more options from a list. It can be used in forms where the options require custom styling [or as a component to filter or sort information].

Put Dropdown in a Field if you need a label, info button, and validation.


🔗 Usage guidance
🔗 Storybook

componentSets.name: Field
componentSets.description:
A field is a combination of a label and any form component, like an input, text area, or dropdown. Optionally, fields can also have info buttons, helper text, and validation states to give people clues about the information they need to enter.


🔗 Usage guidance
🔗 Storybook

componentSets.name: InfoLabel
componentSets.description:
InfoLabel is a combination of a label and info button. When people interact with the info button, the information is surfaced in a Popover. Because the popover isn’t always visible, don’t include information that people must know in order to complete the field. To give people a hint about how to fill in a field, or let them know what values can be entered, try placeholder or helper text instead.

componentSets.name: Input
componentSets.description:
An input allows people to enter short, free form text data.

If you need to collect more than one line of information, try a textarea.

componentSets.name: Interaction tag
componentSets.description:
A tag is a representation of a value that someone has picked, like recipients for an email or categories on a planner task.
Tags create a visual pattern that lets people know they can change or remove the selection. To show system-generated data that people can’t change, use a badge instead.

componentSets.description:
Labels give a name to a component or group of components. Pair them with components like checkboxes and inputs to prompt someone to enter certain information, or with plaintext to categorize information.  
If you need a label with an info button, consider InfoLabel. If you are are combining Label, any form component and need helper text and validation, consider Field.

componentSets.name: LayoutGrid_Card
componentSets.description:
LayoutGrid is a component created to enhance the use of the swappable instances and multiple object layouts. This is maintained to address the limitation on figma where components can't be nested into other components.
The following components are the same
LayoutGrid_Card
LayoutGrid_Section
The recommended nesting on a page layout is
LayoutGrid_Section > LayoutGrid_Card

The modal dialog is used for a multi-stepped process that isn’t an initial FRE experience. It traps focus to the container while keeping the user’s context to the page with the darkened background. This is a great component for teams who need to let users select a trial, buy, upgrade or input a license or watch videos.


This component is currently not available in code.

componentSets.description:
A popover is a small surface that appears when someone interacts with a component to give nonessential, contextual information without blocking them.

Popovers can have structured content and interactive components. If you need to show a more complex layout or block the page behind, try a dialog. For unstructured plain text, try a tooltip.

componentSets.name: Tree item
componentSets.description:
By default, indentation for tree items is added in increments of 24px. Use the Level sub property to set indentation.


Tree supports 10 levels of indentation out of the box. To change what level of indentation your item is, scroll down to the Layer section and click on the Level dropdown.


When using multiple tree items in a container, be sure to add 2px of gap between tree items to match what is in code.
